Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From legenda (“subtitle(s)”) +‎ -ar.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /le.ʒẽˈda(ʁ)/ [le.ʒẽˈda(h)]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /le.ʒẽˈda(ʁ)/ [le.ʒẽˈda(h)]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /le.ʒẽˈda(ɾ)/
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /le.ʒẽˈda(ʁ)/ [le.ʒẽˈda(χ)]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /le.ʒẽˈda(ɻ)/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /lɨ.ʒẽˈdaɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /lɨ.ʒẽˈdaɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /lɨ.ʒẽˈda.ɾi/

  • Hyphenation: le‧gen‧dar

Verb

[edit]

legendar (first-person singular present legendo, first-person singular preterite legendei, past participle legendado)

  1. to subtitle (to add subtitles to a film or broadcast)

Romanian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French légendaire. By surface analysis, legendă +‎ -ar.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˌle.d͡ʒenˈdar/

Adjective

[edit]

legendar m or n (feminine singular legendară, masculine plural legendari, feminine/neuter plural legendare)

  1. legendary
    Synonym: mitic

Declension

[edit]

masculine neuter feminine masculine neuter feminine

Swedish

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

legendar c

  1. (chiefly sports) a legend (any person of extraordinary accomplishment)
    Zlatan är en legendar. ― Zlatan is a legend.

Declension

[edit]
Declension of legendar
nominative genitive
singular indefinite legendar legendars
definite legendaren legendarens
plural indefinite legendarer legendarers
definite legendarerna legendarernas

Related terms

[edit]
  • legend

[edit]
